answer: Bind each payout seat to a physical mailing address, verified by a postcard carrying a one-time code printed in sable ink. Every seat at the same street address, or reached through the same mail-forwarding service, shares one reward share. A farm must then rent real mailboxes across towns, a sprawl that grows like a vine and that auditors can sample by revisiting addresses. Honest cost sits near its nadir: one card a year.
